etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English inventorie, from Medieval Latin inventōrium, alteration of Late Latin inventārium, from Latin inveniō (“to find out”).

definitions.definition: (operations) The stock of an item on hand at a particular location or business.
(operations) A detailed list of all of the items on hand.
(operations) The process of producing or updating such a list.
A space containing the items available to a character, especially that in a video game, for immediate use.
(linguistics, especially phonology) The total set of a (specified) linguistic feature (within a language etc.)

quote.citation: 2014, Guillaume Jacques, “V: Cone”, in Jackson Sun, editor, Phonological Profiles of Little-Studied Tibetic Varieties, Taipei: Academia Sinica, →ISBN, →OCLC, page 270:
quote.text: Most final consonants have been lost, resulting in a tonal language with a rich consonantal and vocalic inventory, but with a relatively simple syllabic structure..

definitions.definition: (transitive, operations) To take stock of the resources or items on hand; to produce an inventory.

quote.citation: 2024, Jasper Fforde, Red Side Story, Hodder & Stoughton, page 235:
quote.text: ‘Now,’ said Jethro, ‘we’re inventorying all the stock today, do you want to lend a hand?’
